verses.text: Tax collectors and people known as sinners kept coming near to Jesus to hear him.
The Pharisees and legal teachers grumbled: “This man welcomes sinners and even eats with them!”
So Jesus told them this parable:
“Which of you, with a hundred sheep, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine out in the open country and go search for the one that got lost until you found it?”
“When you find it, you joyfully lift it onto your shoulders.”
“When you get home, you call your friends and neighbors and say, ‘Celebrate with me! I found my lost sheep!’”
“I’m telling you, heaven will have more joy over one sinner who turns back to God than over ninety-nine righteous people who don’t think they need to repent.”
“Or suppose a woman has ten drachma coins and loses one. Won’t she light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it?”
“When she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors: ‘Celebrate with me! I found the drachma I lost!’”
“In the same way, I’m telling you, God’s angels celebrate when one sinner turns back to God.”
Then Jesus said, “A man had two sons.”
“The younger son said to his father, ‘Father, give me the share of the property that’s coming to me.’ So the father divided his livelihood between his sons.”
“A few days later, the younger son gathered everything he had and went to a distant country. There he blew through his property, living recklessly.”
“After he’d spent it all, a severe famine hit that country, and he was in real need.”
“He went and hired himself out to one of the people there, who sent him to the fields to feed pigs.”
“He was so hungry he wanted to eat the pods the pigs were eating, but nobody gave him anything.”
“Then he came to his senses and thought, ‘My father’s hired workers have more than enough food, and I’m starving to death!’”
“He said, ‘I’ll get up and go to my father. I’ll say, “Father, I’ve sinned against heaven and against you.”’”
“‘I’m no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me one of your hired workers.’”
“So he got up and went to his father. While he was still far away, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to him, threw his arms around him, and kissed him.”
“The son said, ‘Father, I’ve sinned against heaven and against you. I’m no longer worthy to be called your son.’”
“But the father told his servants, ‘Quick, bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.”
“‘Bring the fattened calf, slaughter it, and let’s eat and celebrate!”
“‘This son of mine was dead, but he’s alive again. He was lost, but now he’s found!’ And the celebration began. 🎉”
“The older son was out in the field. As he came near the house, he heard music and dancing.”
He called one of the servants over and asked what was happening.
The servant said, ‘Your brother came home, and your father slaughtered the fattened calf because he got him back safe and sound.’
“The older brother got angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.”
“But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I’ve worked for you and never disobeyed one of your commands. You never even gave me a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.”
“‘But when this son of yours comes back after blowing your money on prostitutes, you slaughter the fattened calf for him!’”
“The father told him, ‘Son, you’re always here with me, and everything I have is yours.”
“‘But we had to celebrate and be glad. This brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”
